why_boundary: Zero is the lower numeric boundary for an expense.
expected_behavior: Define policy; default reject zero as not a positive expense and show a validation error.

why_boundary: A negative amount may represent a refund, but the schema has no transaction type.
expected_behavior: Define policy; default reject negative amounts rather than silently treating them as expenses.

why_boundary: An extremely large value can exceed numeric storage or display capacity; no maximum is specified.
expected_behavior: Reject values outside the supported numeric range with a validation error; define and document that range.

why_boundary: The amount has more fractional digits than the usual USD minor unit.
expected_behavior: Define policy; default reject unsupported fractional precision instead of silently rounding.

why_boundary: A required numeric field is null; missing, empty, and whitespace-only amounts are equivalent boundary variants.
expected_behavior: Reject the entry and identify amount as required.

why_boundary: The amount is malformed text rather than an unambiguous decimal value.
expected_behavior: Reject the entry with an amount-format validation error; do not guess a locale or reinterpret separators.

why_boundary: Exercises just below, exactly at, and just above 2 times a same-category average of 50.00.
expected_behavior: Flag only 100.01: the stated rule is strictly more than 2 times the average; do not flag 99.99 or 100.00.

why_boundary: The average is zero, making the comparison boundary explicit without division.
expected_behavior: Define zero-average policy; default apply amount > 2 × average, so 0.00 is not flagged and 0.01 is flagged.

why_boundary: A required currency is null; empty and whitespace-only currency values are equivalent variants.
expected_behavior: Reject the entry and identify currency as required.

why_boundary: Lowercase input tests normalization of a code-like currency value.
expected_behavior: Define policy; default accept valid ISO 4217 codes case-insensitively and store/display the canonical uppercase code.

why_boundary: A symbol-plus-markup string is not a valid currency code and tests untrusted input handling.
expected_behavior: Reject as an unsupported currency code; render the submitted text safely if shown in an error.

why_boundary: A syntactically code-shaped but likely unsupported currency is paired with an unlisted category; category configurability is unspecified.
expected_behavior: Define supported-currency and category policies; default reject unsupported currencies and accept non-empty user-defined categories.

why_boundary: Whitespace-only category is visually empty despite containing characters.
expected_behavior: Reject the entry and identify category as required; trim surrounding whitespace before validating.

why_boundary: Unicode, combining characters, emoji, and surrounding spaces test category normalization and encoding.
expected_behavior: Accept a non-empty category, preserve valid Unicode, and trim surrounding whitespace; do not corrupt or conflate distinct labels.

why_boundary: An unusually long category may exceed storage or UI limits; no category-length limit is specified.
expected_behavior: Define and document a category-length limit; default reject over-limit text with a clear message rather than silently truncating.

why_boundary: Two adjacent dates straddle a calendar-month boundary.
expected_behavior: Include June 30 only in June's Food total and July 1 only in July's Food total.

why_boundary: February 29 is valid in a leap year and tests the calendar edge.
expected_behavior: Accept the valid leap date and aggregate it into February 2024.

why_boundary: February 29 is invalid in a non-leap year.
expected_behavior: Reject the entry with a date validation error.

why_boundary: A required date is null; missing, empty, and whitespace-only date values are equivalent variants.
expected_behavior: Reject the entry and identify date as required.

why_boundary: A slash-separated date differs from the assumed ISO YYYY-MM-DD date-only format.
expected_behavior: Define accepted input formats; default require a real date in YYYY-MM-DD and reject this value rather than guessing.

why_boundary: Note is optional; null, missing, empty, and whitespace-only values test its absence behavior.
expected_behavior: Accept the expense and treat the note as absent; do not substitute a misleading note.

why_boundary: Emoji and right-to-left and CJK text exercise Unicode storage and rendering.
expected_behavior: Accept and preserve the note's Unicode text and directionality.

why_boundary: A very long note may exceed storage or UI limits; no note-length limit is specified.
expected_behavior: Define and document a note-length limit; default reject over-limit text with a clear message rather than silently truncating.

why_boundary: Markup-like characters, quotes, and punctuation are untrusted display text, not executable content.
expected_behavior: Accept as literal text if otherwise valid; escape it in every rendered context and never interpret it as markup or a command.

why_boundary: Combines the smallest positive amount, a less-used category, leap day, and Unicode note in one otherwise valid expense.
expected_behavior: Accept if 0.01 is valid for the selected currency; preserve the date and note and include it once in the February Travel total.

why_boundary: Repeated same-category entries and a month transition exercise grouping and monthly summation.
expected_behavior: June Food total is USD 30.00 and July Food total is USD 5.00; keep months separate.

why_boundary: A category's monthly entries use different currencies and cannot be safely added as a single numeric total without exchange-rate rules.
expected_behavior: Define conversion policy; absent exchange rates, show separate monthly totals by currency and do not sum unlike currencies.

why_boundary: Identical submissions in sequence test duplicate handling; the schema has no transaction identifier or idempotency key.
expected_behavior: Define duplicate policy; default record each accepted submission once and total USD 20.00 because the data cannot establish that either is accidental.

why_boundary: A burst of many small entries checks that aggregation does not drop or multiply records.
expected_behavior: Process all 1,000 entries and report a June Food total of USD 10.00; surface an explicit error if volume limits are exceeded.

why_boundary: The unusual-spending rule has no average on first use.
expected_behavior: Define minimum-history policy; default do not flag until a usable same-category average exists, and still record and total the expense.
